Nearly Three-Quarters (71%) of College-Aged Students are Registered to Vote; They Say They'd Elect George W. Bush for President if Election Were Tomorrow

NEW YORK, Feb. 28 /PRNewswire/ -- When LINK Magazine asks -- students answer. As election time is fast-approaching, nearly three quarters (71 %) of the students are in fact registered to vote and 27% say they'd cast their vote for George W. Bush as the next President of the United States. These findings are from the first in a series of LINK INDEX surveys, which polls nearly 500 college students throughout the country who are readers of LINK Magazine.

Sixty-percent of the respondents are not affected by allegations towards Bush about his drug use or extramarital affairs. In addition, two-thirds of the students feel their vote matters at the election polls.

Students also weighed in on hot political issues. The survey reveals that 18-24 year olds say they ``somewhat approve'' of the job President Clinton is doing; 53% identify education as the most important issue; 49% are pro-choice with no exceptions; 36% feel that marijuana should remain illegal; and 42% feel that leadership is the most important quality in a politician.

(MarijuanaNews note: That is an odd way of reporting the results on marijuana. Perhaps they were afraid that if they reported that 64% thought that marijuana should be legalized that would get more attention than the rest of the survey. Although there are usually some who are " undecided " in any survey, it would seem that a clear majority favor legalization, and that would be politically incorrect. Very interesting. We are winning on the campuses. In any case, marijuana is more popular than George W. Bush, and far less dangerous.)

LINK Magazine, a property of the CTN Media Group (Nasdaq: UCTN), is direct-mailed into student mailboxes at more than 600 schools nationwide, with a one million, ABC-audited circulation.

CTN Media Group is the nation's #1 media gateway for reaching young adults. CTN Media Group is the parent company to College Television Network, the country's fastest growing young adult television network; LINK Magazine, the nation's most widely read college magazine; and Market Place Media, the leading media placement and promotion company reaching targeted markets. CTN Media Group's properties offer marketers an opportunity to reach nearly half of all young adults between 18 and 24. CTN's fast growth has attracted significant investment partners. Willis Stein & Partners, a leading private equity firm, is the controlling shareholder in CTN. Willis Stein & Partners specializes in investments with media communications companies.
